mainTopic: Shabbat 109a: morning hand-washing and eye care, then what counts as forbidden רפואה on שבת: foods, drinks, soaking wounds, and bathing in healing waters
overview: This amud opens at the end of a list of dangers from touching things with unwashed hands in the morning. It adds רבי נתן's teaching that the harmful spirit leaves only after washing three times, and רבי יוחנן's teaching on the benefits of פוך. The גמרא then turns to healing on שבת. It names items that are not medicine: leaves, coriander and hops (except טרוזא). It discusses which drinks are permitted, with a story about זעירי's wife and זעירי's reasoning. מר עוקבא permits soaking a wound in wine but not vinegar, and רבא limits this for the delicate people of מחוזא. A story about רב אשי soaking his foot teaches that a wound on the back of the hand or foot is dangerous enough to break שבת for. Finally, two ברייתות disagree about bathing in the Great Sea on שבת. רבי יוחנן explains that they follow רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה. רב נחמן בר יצחק begins to challenge this, and his challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the list of dangers from unwashed hands
steps.stepSummary: The list of dangers from touching things with unwashed morning hands finishes: a hand that touches a beer barrel, the eyes, the ears or the nose.
steps.simpleTranslation: A hand that touches a barrel should be cut off. A hand on the eye blinds, a hand on the ear deafens, a hand on the nose or mouth brings up polyps.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a list, which began on the previous page, of the harm caused by touching things before washing in the morning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that a harmful spirit rests on the hands before morning washing. Touching a barrel ruins the beer. Touching the eye, ear or nose causes physical damage to that organ.

keyTerms.meaning: a barrel or vat, here of beer
should be cut off (strong language of warning)
polyps, a growth in the nose

steps.confusionAlert: "תיקצץ" is not a real punishment. It is strong language meaning "this hand is dangerous and must be kept away."

phrases.english: [a hand placed] into a barrel should be severed,
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the previous page: putting a hand in the barrel keeps the beer from fermenting properly.

phrases.english: a hand [on the eye] blinds, a hand [on the ear] deafens,
a hand [on the nose or mouth] brings up polyps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continuation of a list from the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unwashed morning hands harm the beer, eyes, ears and nose.

steps.title: רבי נתן: the spirit leaves only after washing three times
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי נתן: the harmful spirit on the hands is stubborn and does not leave until one washes three times.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי נתן says, this spirit is a free and independent one, and it insists on staying until a person washes his hands three times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא explaining how to remove the harmful spirit from the hands: wash them three times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 told us the danger. Here we learn the remedy: one washing is not enough, three are needed. This is the source for washing the hands three times in the morning (נטילת ידים שחרית).

keyTerms.meaning: a free woman; here, an independent, stubborn spirit

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic source for the practice of washing each hand three times on waking.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Natan says:
This [spirit] is a free one,
and she insists [on staying] until he washes
his hands three times.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the remedy for the danger described in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The spirit on the hands leaves only after washing three times.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן on the benefits of eye shadow
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says פוך (eye shadow) drives away the spirit called בת מלך, stops tears and grows eyelashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: eye shadow removes the spirit called "the King's Daughter," stops tearing, and makes the eyelashes grow.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן lists three benefits of putting פוך on the eyes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the theme of eye care and harmful spirits. Note that פוך is described as having real benefits. That matters for the surrounding שבת laws about what counts as treatment.

keyTerms.meaning: "the King's Daughter," the name of a harmful spirit or eye ailment

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Eye shadow removes the "Daughter of the King,"
and stops tears,
and increases hair on the eyelids.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: פּוּךְ מַעֲבִיר בַּת מֶלֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related teaching about the eyes and harmful spirits.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פוך removes בת מלך, stops tears and grows eyelashes.

steps.title: A ברייתא from רבי יוסי supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יוסי saying the exact same three benefits of פוך, which supports רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: רבי יוסי says, eye shadow removes the King's Daughter, stops tears and grows eyelashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that an earlier source (a ברייתא) says the same thing as רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase "תניא נמי הכי" introduces support from a תנא. רבי יוסי's words match רבי יוחנן's word for word. So רבי יוחנן's statement has an earlier, authoritative basis.

keyTerms.meaning: it was also taught this way (introduces a supporting ברייתא)

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was also taught so: Rabbi Yosei says:
Eye shadow removes the "Daughter of the King,"
and stops tears,
and increases hair on the eyelids.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 3 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי יוסי with identical wording.

steps.title: Leaves, coriander and hops are not medicine
steps.stepSummary: שמואל, רב יוסף and רב ששת each name an item that is not considered רפואה, so using it on שבת is not forbidden healing.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר עוקבא said in the name of שמואל: leaves have no healing power. רב יוסף said: coriander has no healing power. רב ששת said: hops have no healing power.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the laws of healing on שבת. It lists three items that are not considered medicine, so using them on שבת is not a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Healing on שבת is forbidden by the חכמים (a גזירה about grinding herbs for medicine). Something that has no real healing effect does not fall under this prohibition. These three statements each remove one item from the category of medicine.

keyTerms.meaning: they have no element of healing (so they are permitted on שבת)

phrases.english: And Mar Ukva said in the name of Shmuel:
Leaves contain no element of healing.
Rav Yosef said:
Coriander contains no element of healing.
Rav Sheshet said:
Hops contain no element of healing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from אגדה about the eyes back to the הלכה of healing on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leaves, coriander and hops are not medicine, so they are permitted on שבת.

steps.title: רב יוסף and רב ששת add personal remarks
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says coriander actually harms him. רב ששת says arugula actually helps him. Both were blind.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: coriander is even bad for me. רב ששת said: arugula is even good for me.
steps.whatsHappening: The two אמוראים who were blind add personal comments to their earlier statements.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף goes further than "coriander does not heal." He says it is actually harmful, even to a blind man like him. רב ששת notes that arugula is good for him even though he is blind.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse "קשיא" here with the גמרא's word for a challenge. Here it simply means "harmful."

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Coriander is harmful even to me.
Rav Sheshet said:
Arugula is beneficial even to me.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: תוספת (addendum), no exact match in the label set
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Personal additions to the statements in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Coriander is even harmful; arugula is beneficial.

steps.title: All hops are permitted except טרוזא
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that every kind of hops may be used on שבת except טרוזא, which is used only as medicine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And מר עוקבא said in the name of שמואל: all kinds of hops are permitted, except טרוזא.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a general permission for hops and makes one exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hops in general are eaten as food, so they are permitted. טרוזא is used only for healing, so it falls under the healing prohibition. The rule is that a food eaten by healthy people is permitted, while an item used only as medicine is not.

keyTerms.meaning: a type of hops used only medicinally

phrases.english: And Mar Ukva said in the name of Shmuel:
All types of hops are permitted
except for teruza.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל מִינֵי כְּשׁוּת שְׁרוּ לְבַר מִטָּרוֹזָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to the permission for hops.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All hops are permitted on שבת except טרוזא.

steps.title: רב חסדא: melon juice permitted, פיעפועי juice forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא permits drinking one kind of juice on שבת and forbids another.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: melon juice is permitted. The juice of פיעפועי is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא rules on two drinks: one permitted, one forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first drink is normally consumed as a regular food, so drinking it is not healing. The גמרא does not state here why the second is forbidden on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: juice of פיעפועים, a type of vegetable

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
Melon juice is permitted,
the juice of pipuim is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: שִׁירְקָא טַוְיָא שְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another ruling on healing foods and drinks on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Melon juice is permitted on שבת; פיעפועי juice is forbidden.

steps.title: זעירי's wife and חייא בר אשי
steps.stepSummary: זעירי's wife made the melon drink for חייא בר אשי, who refused it. She pointed out that his teacher זעירי had eaten it.
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירי's wife made it for חייא בר אשי, and he did not eat. She said to him: I made it for your teacher and he ate it, and you will not eat?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing a dispute in practice: זעירי ate the drink on שבת, but his student refused. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חייא בר אשי was worried that consuming it was forbidden healing. His teacher זעירי had no such worry. The next step explains why זעירי permitted it.

phrases.english: Ze'iri's wife made it
for Chiyya bar Ashi, and he did not eat.
She said to him:
I made it for your teacher and he ate,
and you do not eat?!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵיתְהוּ דִּזְעֵירִי עֲבַדָא לֵיהּ לְחִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story about the permitted drink from step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זעירי ate the drink on שבת; his student refused it.

steps.title: זעירי follows his own reasoning about the strainer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that זעירי permitted the drink because of his rule about straining clear wine: if something is consumed as-is anyway, you are not really doing anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירי follows his own reasoning, since זעירי said: a person may pour clear wine and clear water into a strainer on שבת without worry. We see that since it is drunk that way anyway, he is not doing anything. Here too, since it is eaten that way anyway, he is not doing anything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why זעירי ate the drink. It shows his ruling matches a different ruling of his about straining wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Straining wine that is already clear is not a forbidden act of sorting, because the wine is drunk as it is anyway. In the same way, a food that people normally eat as food is not an act of healing. זעירי's view is consistent across both cases.

keyTerms.meaning: according to his own reasoning (consistent with his other ruling)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a general principle: an act that changes nothing meaningful does not count as a forbidden act on שבת.

phrases.english: Ze'iri follows his own reasoning,
as Ze'iri said:

phrases.aramaic: נוֹתֵן אָדָם יַיִן צָלוּל וּמַיִם צְלוּלִין
phrases.english: A person may put clear wine and clear water
into a strainer on Shabbat, without concern.
Apparently, since it is drunk this way [anyway],
he is not doing anything;
here too, since it is eaten this way [anyway],
he is not doing anything.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains זעירי's behavior in the story of step 9.
steps.raayaObject: זעירי's permission to consume the drink on שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: זעירי's own ruling about pouring clear wine into a strainer.

steps.title: מר עוקבא: a wound may be soaked in wine
steps.stepSummary: מר עוקבא rules that someone with a wounded hand or foot may soak it in wine on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And מר עוקבא said: one whose hand or foot was struck may soak it in wine and need not worry.
steps.whatsHappening: מר עוקבא permits soaking a wound in wine on שבת to stop the bleeding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine is a normal drink and is not seen as medicine. So soaking a wound in it does not look like forbidden healing.

phrases.english: And Mar Ukva said:
One whose hand or foot was wounded
may soak it in wine and need not be concerned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new healing case about wounds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wound may be soaked in wine on שבת.

steps.title: What about vinegar?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask whether a wound may be soaked in vinegar instead of wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: what about vinegar?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether מר עוקבא's permission for wine also covers vinegar. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vinegar is stronger and stings, so it may count as real medicine. The question is whether it is like wine or not.

keyTerms.meaning: they asked (a question raised in the בית מדרש)

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
What about vinegar?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether step 11 extends to vinegar.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May a wound be soaked in vinegar on שבת?

steps.title: In רב כהנא's house they said vinegar is not allowed
steps.stepSummary: רב הלל reports that in רב כהנא's בית מדרש they ruled vinegar is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הלל said to רב אשי: when I was in רב כהנא's house, they said vinegar is not permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הלל answers the question: vinegar may not be used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vinegar heals strongly and is clearly medicine, unlike wine. So it falls under the prohibition of healing on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: the house (study hall) of רב כהנא

phrases.english: Rav Hillel said to Rav Ashi:
When I was in Rav Kahana's house
they said: vinegar, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֲוֵינָא בֵּי רַב כָּהֲנָא אָמְרִי חַלָּא לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Vinegar is not permitted for soaking a wound on שבת.

steps.title: רבא: for the delicate people of מחוזא, even wine heals
steps.stepSummary: רבא limits מר עוקבא's rule: for the delicate people of מחוזא, wine itself works as medicine, so they may not soak wounds in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: and these people of מחוזא, since they are delicate, even wine heals them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds an exception to the wine permission for people with sensitive bodies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether something counts as medicine depends on its effect on the person. For delicate people, wine has a real healing effect, so for them it is like vinegar and is forbidden. The category of wine stays the same; only the result changes for these people.

keyTerms.meaning: the people of מחוזא, a wealthy town

steps.whatToRemember: Wine on a wound is permitted on שבת because it is not considered medicine. Vinegar is forbidden. For delicate people, even wine counts as healing and is forbidden. The test is whether the substance actually works as medicine for this person.

phrases.english: Rava said:
And these people of Mechoza,
since they are delicate,
even wine heals them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the wine permission of step 11 for delicate people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For the delicate people of מחוזא, wine counts as medicine, so they may not soak wounds in it on שבת.

steps.title: רבינא sees רב אשי soaking his injured foot in vinegar
steps.stepSummary: A story: רבינא visits רב אשי and sees him soaking his foot in vinegar on שבת after a donkey stepped on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא happened to come to רב אשי's house. He saw that a donkey had stepped on the back of רב אשי's foot, and רב אשי was sitting and soaking it in vinegar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that sets up a question. It describes what רבינא saw so that he can challenge it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 13, רב הלל reported that soaking a wound in vinegar on שבת is forbidden. Here a major אמורא is seen doing exactly that. This story creates the tension that the next steps will resolve.

keyTerms.meaning: on the back of his foot

phrases.english: Ravina happened to come to the house of Rav Ashi.
He saw that a donkey had stepped on him,
on the back of his foot,
and he was sitting and soaking it in vinegar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a real-life case that seems to clash with רב הלל's ruling in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative fact: רב אשי soaked his injured foot in vinegar on שבת.

steps.title: רבינא asks: doesn't רב הלל forbid vinegar?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges רב אשי with רב הלל's report that vinegar is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to him: Doesn't the Master agree with what רב הלל said, that vinegar is not allowed?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges רב אשי's behavior, using the ruling from step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vinegar on a wound works as real medicine, so soaking a wound in it counts as healing on שבת, which the רבנן forbade. רבינא wants to know how רב אשי can do it.

keyTerms.meaning: Doesn't the Master hold (this view)? A polite way of challenging a teacher.
the אמורא who reported that vinegar is forbidden

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר
phrases.english: He said to him: Doesn't the Master hold
according to what Rav Hillel said:
vinegar is not allowed?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר לְהָא דְּאָמַר רַב הִילֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the story into a challenge based on step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's act of soaking his foot in vinegar
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב הלל reported that vinegar is forbidden, yet רב אשי used it.

steps.title: רב אשי answers: the back of the hand and foot is different
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that a wound on the back of the hand or foot is a special case.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The back of the hand and the back of the foot are different.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge by saying his injury is a special exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי does agree with רב הלל's rule for ordinary wounds. A wound on the back of the hand or foot, however, is dangerous. Because of that danger, healing it on שבת is allowed.
steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not arguing with רב הלל. He agrees that vinegar is normally forbidden. He is only saying that his kind of wound is an exception.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: גַּב הַיָּד וְגַב הָרֶגֶל שָׁאנֵי.
phrases.english: He said to him: The back of the hand and the back of the foot are different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (an exception for a dangerous location)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אשי was going against רב הלל's ban on vinegar.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban applies to ordinary wounds. A wound on the back of the hand or foot is dangerous, so it may be treated.

steps.title: Another version: רב אשי was soaking his foot in wine
steps.stepSummary: A second version of the story says רב אשי was soaking his foot in wine, not vinegar.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say that רבינא saw רב אשי soaking his foot in wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a different version of the same story. It is setting up a different challenge, this time based on רבא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine is normally allowed (מר עוקבא, step 11). But רבא said that for delicate people of מחוזא, wine counts as medicine (step 14). So this version leads to a challenge from רבא instead of from רב הלל.

phrases.english: Some say:
he saw that he was soaking it in wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Retells the story of step 15 with wine instead of vinegar.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Alternate version: רב אשי soaked his foot in wine.

steps.title: רבינא asks: aren't you delicate like the people of מחוזא?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges רב אשי using רבא's rule that wine heals delicate people, and he says רב אשי is also delicate.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to him: Doesn't the Master agree with what רבא said, that the people of מחוזא are delicate, so even wine heals them? And the Master is also delicate!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges רב אשי using רבא's limit from step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a delicate person, wine works as real medicine, so soaking a wound in it counts as forbidden healing. רב אשי was wealthy and delicate, so רבא's limit should apply to him too.

keyTerms.meaning: מחוזא, a wealthy city whose residents were known as delicate

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר
phrases.english: He said to him: Doesn't the Master hold
according to what Rava said:
These people of Mechoza, since they are delicate,
even wine also heals them?
And the Master is also delicate!

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר לְהָא דְּאָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wine version using step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי soaking his foot in wine
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא forbade delicate people to soak wounds in wine, and רב אשי is delicate.

steps.title: רב אשי answers again: a wound on the back of the hand or foot is like a life-threatening wound
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives the same answer and backs it up with רב's ruling that such wounds are dangerous enough to break שבת for.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The back of the hand and the back of the foot are different. As רב אדא בר מתנה said in the name of רב: The back of the hand and the back of the foot are like a life-threatening wound, and one may break שבת for them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives the same answer as before. This time he supports it with a source from רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב teaches that a wound on the back of the hand or foot counts as a מכה של חלל, a life-threatening wound. For a life-threatening wound you may even break שבת. So the ordinary rabbinic ban on healing does not apply, whether one uses wine or vinegar.

keyTerms.meaning: the אמורא who reports רב's ruling

steps.whatToRemember: Normally, healing on שבת with clearly medicinal methods (like vinegar, or wine for delicate people) is forbidden. A wound on the back of the hand or foot is treated as dangerous, so treating it is fully allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source in the גמרא for treating wounds on the back of the hand or foot as a case of פיקוח נפש on שבת.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: גַּב הַיָּד וְגַב הָרֶגֶל שָׁאנֵי.
phrases.english: He said to him: The back of the hand and the back of the foot are different.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: As Rav Adda bar Mattana said that Rav said:
The back of the hand and the back of the foot
are like a life-threatening wound,
and one may desecrate Shabbat for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּב הַיָּד וְגַב הָרֶגֶל שָׁאנֵי, דְּאָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19 and gives the source for the answer in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case, supported by a quoted ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אשי, a delicate person, was going against רבא's limit.
steps.terutzMaskana: A wound on the back of the hand or foot is life-threatening, so treating it overrides שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב אדא בר מתנה in the name of רב

steps.title: A ברייתא lists which healing waters one may bathe in on שבת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא allows bathing on שבת in hot springs like those of טבריה, but forbids the Great Sea, flax-soaking water, and the Dead Sea.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: One may bathe on שבת in the waters of גרר, חמתן, עסיא, and טבריה, but not in the Great Sea, not in water used for soaking flax, and not in the Sea of סדום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes a ברייתא about bathing in healing waters on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People bathe in hot springs for pleasure too, so bathing there does not look like healing, and it is allowed. The forbidden waters are used only for medical treatment, so bathing in them looks like healing on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: water in which flax was soaked

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One may bathe in the waters of Gerar, in the waters of Chamatan,
in the waters of Asya and in the waters of Tiberias,
but not in the Great Sea,
nor in flax-soaking water,
nor in the Sea of Sodom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic that stays within the theme of healing on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bathing in hot springs is allowed. Bathing in the Great Sea, flax water, and the Dead Sea is forbidden.

steps.title: A second ברייתא contradicts the first about the Great Sea
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא allows bathing in the Great Sea, which contradicts the first ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the גמרא points out a contradiction: Another ברייתא says one may bathe in the waters of טבריה and in the Great Sea, but not in flax-soaking water and not in the Sea of סדום. So the ruling on the Great Sea in one ברייתא contradicts the ruling on the Great Sea in the other!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets two ברייתות side by side and shows that they disagree about the Great Sea. The answer will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות agree about flax water and the Dead Sea. The only clash is the Great Sea: the first ברייתא forbids it and the second allows it.

keyTerms.meaning: and they contrasted them (introduces a contradicting source)

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
One may bathe in the waters of Tiberias and in the Great Sea,
but not in flax-soaking water,
nor in the Sea of Sodom.
This is difficult: the Great Sea contradicts the Great Sea!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא of step 21 with a contradicting ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first ברייתא's ban on bathing in the Great Sea
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא explicitly allows bathing in the Great Sea.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says the two ברייתות follow different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן resolves the contradiction: the ברייתא that permits bathing in the Great Sea follows רבי מאיר, and the one that forbids it follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: This is not difficult. This ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, and that ברייתא follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the contradiction from Step 22. He says the two ברייתות are not arguing with each other by mistake. Each one simply follows a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר treats all seas as the same, so the Great Sea is just ordinary sea water, and bathing in it is allowed. רבי יהודה treats the Great Sea as different from other seas, so it gets grouped with the forbidden waters. The source showing this disagreement is brought in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no real contradiction
This one ... that one (pointing to two different sources)
A תנא who holds that all seas are the same
A תנא who holds that the Great Sea is unique

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up which ברייתא goes with which תנא. The ברייתא that PERMITS bathing in the Great Sea follows רבי מאיר, who says all seas are alike. The ברייתא that FORBIDS it follows רבי יהודה, who says the Great Sea is special.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: it is not difficult:
this one is Rabbi Meir,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא that permits bathing in the Great Sea.

phrases.english: that one is Rabbi Yehuda.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא that forbids bathing in the Great Sea.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction between the two ברייתות raised in Step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: תנאי היא: each source follows a different תנא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the two ברייתות contradict each other about the Great Sea.
steps.terutzMaskana: They reflect a real מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה about whether the Great Sea is like all other seas.

steps.title: The משנה where רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה disagree about seas as a מקוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן quotes a משנה. There, רבי מאיר says all seas purify like a מקוה, while רבי יהודה says only the Great Sea does.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: All seas purify like a מקוה, as the פסוק says, 'and the gathering of the waters (מקוה) He called seas.' These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: Only the Great Sea is like a מקוה. The פסוק says 'seas' only because the Great Sea contains many kinds of seas.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן brings a source to prove that רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה really do disagree about the Great Sea. The source is a משנה about which seas can be used as a מקוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר reads the plural word 'seas' as including every sea, so all seas are alike. רבי יהודה says the plural refers to the many seas inside the Great Sea itself, so the Great Sea stands apart from the others. This gives the basis for saying רבי יהודה would treat bathing in the Great Sea differently.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
A gathering of water used for ritual purification

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא technique. A contradiction between two sources is solved by finding a known מחלוקת elsewhere and assigning each source to one side.

phrases.english: As we learned: all seas are like a ritual bath,
as it says: 'and the gathering of the waters He called seas,'
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: יָם הַגָּדוֹל כְּמִקְוֶה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: the Great Sea is like a ritual bath,
phrases.notes: Only the Great Sea, not other seas.

phrases.english: and the verse only says 'seas'

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ מִינֵי יַמִּים הַרְבֵּה.
phrases.english: because there are many kinds of seas in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source behind רבי יוחנן's answer in Step 23.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה disagree about whether the Great Sea is like other seas.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה about seas as a מקוה (משנה מקואות ה:ד).

steps.title: רבי יוסי's view on the purifying power of seas
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה continues with רבי יוסי. He says all seas purify even when the water is flowing, but sea water cannot be used for זבים, מצורעים, or for making מי חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: All seas purify even when flowing. But they are invalid for זבים, for מצורעים, and for sanctifying מי חטאת with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the same משנה, which adds a third opinion from רבי יוסי. This part completes the quote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular מקוה only purifies when its water is still. רבי יוסי says seas purify even when the water is moving. Still, sea water does not count as the 'living' spring water that a זב, a מצורע, and מי חטאת require, so it cannot be used for those.

keyTerms.meaning: People with a certain bodily discharge who need spring water to become pure
Purification water mixed with the ashes of the פרה אדומה

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי makes seas MORE powerful than a מקוה in one way, since they work even when flowing. But he makes them LESS powerful in another way, since they are not valid where spring water is required. Both points are true at once.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
all seas purify even when flowing,
phrases.notes: Unlike a מקוה, which must be still.

phrases.english: and they are invalid for zavim and for lepers
and for sanctifying purification water with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הַיַּמִּים מְטַהֲרִין בְּזוֹחֲלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה quoted in Step 24 with a third opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seas purify even when flowing, but they are invalid where spring water is required (זבים, מצורעים, מי חטאת).

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק begins to challenge רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק opens a strong objection to רבי יוחנן's explanation. The content of the objection comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק strongly objects to this:
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. רב נחמן בר יצחק is about to attack רבי יוחנן's answer, and the actual challenge follows in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מתקיף לה signals a forceful challenge to the answer just given, which here means linking the ברייתות to רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה. The opening formula alone does not reveal the argument yet, so the learner should keep reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Strongly objects to it (introduces a forceful challenge)
An אמורא who challenges רבי יוחנן's answer

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak strongly objects to this:

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a challenge to רבי יוחנן's resolution from Steps 23-24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that the two ברייתות follow רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only the opening formula appears here. The actual argument comes on the next amud.
